_comment: Issue #1390. Registers axis 1's PER-FILE check inside check-skill-coverage-map.py: the sub-check that must notice a change to a file OTHER than SKILL.md (most load-bearingly reference.md, where the generator's progressive-disclosure split moves most of a skill's actual instructions) shipped under codex/skills/<skill>/, and report it as stale (content) rather than missing it entirely. A SEPARATE registration from controls/check-skill-coverage-map (axis 2's snapshot-staleness detector) because disabling THIS behavior does not make that control's anchor blind, and disabling THAT one does not make this one's anchor blind - they are independent properties of the same gate, the same shape as this repository's flow-finish-gate family (row 1, ADR 0008).
limits: Covers only axis 1's whole-closure per-file comparison (#1390) - the check that catches a change to reference.md or any other shipped file besides SKILL.md's description/body. Both cases hold axis 2 CURRENT (the fixture's diagnose.closure_digests matches the current tree exactly) so axis 2 cannot mask or substitute for what this control isolates. Fixtures are CONSTRUCTED, not vendored from a real skillc run - the reference digests and diagnose() result are synthetic JSON built to the schema check-skill-coverage-map.py reads. Declared gap: this control does not exercise the added/removed sub-cases (a file present in one side but not the other) - those are pinned by tests/test_skill_coverage_map.py (test_stale_content_new_bundled_file_added, test_stale_content_reference_file_removed) instead, which the ADR 0008 bound does not require a registered control for.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the real pre-#1390 behavior, reproduced exactly - the per-file comparison block (reference_files/current_digests/file_diffs) removed, reverting axis 1 to comparing only description_digest/body_digest, exactly as the gate read before this issue. On bad-reference-md-changed-not-detected (reference.md edited on disk, SKILL.md and axis 2 both still agreeing) the anchor reports `current`/exit 0 instead of `stale (content)`/exit 1 - the real-world defect #1390 reports: 'axis1: current ... axis2: null ... state: unknown' on main, with the remedy pointing at the wrong axis. On good-current it agrees with the real gate (`current`/exit 0), so the miss is isolated to the removed per-file check and not a generally broken gate.
